subject.title: [Feature]: Support for sandbox Docker parameters (--gpus all, --ipc=host)

question: Should OpenClaw expose host IPC for Docker sandboxes, and if yes should it be a narrow explicit `sandbox.docker.ipc` break-glass field instead of raw Docker argument passthrough?
rationale: The remaining request changes the sandbox isolation boundary and public config contract; current code proves GPU is already solved but does not settle whether host IPC should exist.

options.title: Add Narrow IPC Break-Glass Field
options.body: Expose a typed opt-in IPC setting with schema, docs, config hashing, Docker create args, security-audit coverage, warnings, and tests while keeping raw Docker args unsupported.

options.title: Reject Host IPC In Core
options.body: Document GPU passthrough as the supported high-power Docker path and keep host IPC unavailable because it weakens sandbox isolation.

options.title: Define Broader Namespace Policy First
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define one policy for IPC, PID, network namespace joins, capabilities, and other dangerous Docker options.

recommendation.title: Add Narrow IPC Break-Glass Field
recommendation.body: Expose a typed opt-in IPC setting with schema, docs, config hashing, Docker create args, security-audit coverage, warnings, and tests while keeping raw Docker args unsupported.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest policy-history signal for namespace-sharing sandbox hardening is steipete's work on container namespace joins and dangerous Docker override handling.
